brief.outcome: Have the Shopify home goods store ready for the Black Friday weekend so the site stays fast, the top two products do not run out, and the weekend brings in $100,000 (last year $84,000) with margin per order above $18.

ambition.goal_beyond: The sale earns profit and repeat buyers, not just a bigger weekend number, and the store has a playbook for the next peak
rungs: Make the store fast and in stock for the weekend
Plan the sale on the decisions behind it: how much stock to order now, which offers (up to 25% off) and how much ad spend each can carry while margin per order stays above $18
Keep it true after the weekend: a readout of what the sale really earned and a saved playbook, so the next peak starts from facts
ambition.judge: Shopify's orders report for the weekend against last year's $84,000 weekend and a margin-per-order figure computed from order data; the Shopify inventory log for stock-outs; page speed and uptime readings on the sale days. Rung 3 depends on the weekend finishing, so it is delivered as the readout and learning stages after the deadline.

brief.deliverable: A sale-ready store: a stock order placed in time, a sale plan with offers and messages launched with the owners' approval, speed and checkout fixes applied, a support plan and a weekend watch, then an honest readout
done: Last year's weekend rebuilt from the order data and its causes (slowdown, stock-out) separated
Stock order for the top two products decided and placed inside the supplier's 3-week lead time, or the gap stated
Offers set at no more than 25% off, each checked against the $18 margin floor
Speed and checkout fixes applied and re-measured before the sale
Sale emails, ads and discounts launched only with approval of each action
Weekend watched with stop rules, then read against last year's $84,000 and the $100,000 target
brief.deadline: Black Friday weekend, about four weeks away; the stock order has to be placed within about a week to land inside the 3-week supplier lead time
guardrails: Top two products do not sell out before Sunday
The store stays up and fast through the sale (no repeat of last year's Friday slowdown)
limits: Meta Ads and Google Ads are reached through exports only, so the owners change ads by hand
Shopify is read-only for us; the owners apply store changes
assets: Last year's Black Friday weekend Shopify report ($84,000)
Meta Ads and Google Ads exports
brief.technical_level: Not stated; the owners decide, so give ready changes to review with plain-language reasons

answers.question: Store and market?
answers.answer: Home goods store on Shopify, US

answers.question: Last year?
answers.answer: Black Friday weekend did $84,000 (Shopify report); the site slowed on Friday morning; the top two products ran out by Saturday

answers.question: Timing?
answers.answer: Black Friday is in about four weeks; the supplier needs three weeks lead time for reorders

answers.question: Offer limits?
answers.answer: Discounts up to 25% are allowed, nothing deeper

answers.question: Tools?
answers.answer: Shopify MCP read access; Meta Ads and Google Ads through exports only; Gorgias for support

answers.question: Target and guardrail?
answers.answer: $100,000 over the weekend while keeping margin per order above $18

answers.question: Data home and who decides?
answers.answer: Keep data in this project; the owner and co-founder decide together

research.approach: Practitioners treat a peak sale as a capacity problem on three fronts that fail separately: stock, site and support. They start from last year's raw orders, hour by hour and product by product, to find what really capped the weekend (here a slowdown and a stock-out), then work backwards from the supplier's lead time to decide stock now, because after that date stock cannot be fixed. They audit app scripts and theme weight against page-speed limits, walk the checkout on mobile with the real discount codes, and stagger email and ad bursts so traffic does not arrive as one spike. Offers are built as a ladder with margin floors per product and a switch rule, not a single deep discount. Support is prepared with answers for the predictable questions (where is my order, stock, returns). On the day they watch a short list of numbers on a schedule with pre-agreed stop rules, and afterwards read the weekend against last year and the market, not just last year.

sources.title: Shopify blog: BFCM checklist
sources.note: Order promotional stock early, choose products by ABC analysis, set up discounts in advance and test them at checkout, test load times and remove unused apps and pop-ups, update the FAQ and prepare support replies.

sources.title: Shopify developer docs: theme performance best practices
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03. Audit app and third-party scripts and remove the ones not worth their cost, defer non-critical scripts, set image sizes to avoid layout shift, do not lazy-load the main image.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Black Friday online spending record, Adobe says
sources.note: US online Black Friday spending was $11.8B, up about 9% on the year before; the market context for a target of $100,000 against $84,000, which is about 19% growth.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center: inventory settings
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03. Turn on inventory tracking per variant and choose how depleted items are handled; counts are the base for any stock cover calculation.

steps.name: Rebuild last year's weekend from the order data
steps.why: Hour-by-hour orders, units and sessions show what capped $84,000: the slowdown, the stock-out or demand.

steps.name: Work back from the lead time to a stock decision
steps.why: With a 3-week supplier lead time the reorder has a last date; after it, only promotion limits can protect stock.

steps.name: Measure and trim site speed and app weight
steps.why: Heavy app scripts and theme code cause slowdowns when traffic arrives together.

steps.name: Set the offer ladder and ad budget against the margin floor
steps.why: A deeper discount sells more units but can push margin per order under $18; the ladder sets which offer runs when.

steps.name: Test what limited last year and rank the readiness work
steps.why: Money and time go to the cause that cost the most, within the days left.

steps.name: Rehearse discounts and checkout before launch
steps.why: A wrongly stacked or failing discount code during the sale is the costliest bug.

steps.name: Prepare support for the predictable questions
steps.why: Tickets about orders and stock spike with the sale and slow replies lose repeat buyers.

steps.name: Run the weekend watch with stop rules, then read it honestly
steps.why: Pre-agreed stop rules let the owners act fast; the readout compares with last year and the market.

pitfalls.text: Ordering stock after the lead-time cut-off and only finding out in the sale.
Stacking a 25% discount on thin-margin products, which grows sales and shrinks profit.
Sending email and ad bursts at the same hour on heavy pages, then blaming the platform for the slowdown.
Comparing only with last year and ignoring that the market grew about 9%.
Leaving the discount and checkout untested until sale day.

stages.name: Pin down the sale goal and the dates
stages.goal: Turn the owners' words into a measured goal, limits, the stock cut-off date and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Rebuild last year's weekend
stages.goal: Pull last year's weekend orders, hourly traffic, ad results, support tickets and today's stock into one CSV set.

checks.name: Order totals for last year's weekend match the $84,000 Shopify report within 2%, or the gap is explained
Hourly rows are present for the whole weekend, or the gap is noted
Anything the owners did not supply (costs, ad exports, tickets) is listed with what it would unlock

stages.name: Work back from the lead time to the stock decision
stages.goal: Check stock counts, forecast demand for the top two products from last year's weekend and trend, and state the last date a reorder lands in time (3 weeks before the sale).

checks.name: On-hand counts are compared with open orders from the supplier, or marked unverified
States the date after which a reorder cannot arrive before the sale (sale date minus 21 days) and how many days remain
Demand is given as a low, expected and high case, not one number

stages.name: Measure site speed and app weight
stages.goal: Measure mobile speed on the home, collection and top product pages, list app scripts by weight, and find what plausibly caused last Friday's slowdown.

checks.name: Mobile load is measured on the home, a collection and both top product pages, with the 2.5 s largest-content limit for each
Every installed app is listed with the scripts it adds and marked keep, cut or test
States the likely cause of last Friday's slowdown with the evidence, or marks it unknown

stages.name: Find what capped last year
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses: how much was lost to the stock-out and to the slowdown, what margin the offers earned, and whether $100,000 is reachable. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the rows it rests on
Shows how the $16,000 gap to $100,000 splits between recovered stock-out sales, recovered slowdown sales and new demand, each with a low and high estimate
Compares the target's growth (about 19%) with the market's reported growth (about 9%) and says what share of the gain must come from better availability and speed
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank the readiness work and the offers
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked cards: stock quantity and order date, offer ladder with a margin floor per product, ad budget and pacing, speed cuts, support plan.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected effect on weekend sales, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
Every offer card shows margin per order at its discount against the $18 floor, or marks margin unknown
No offer is deeper than 25%
Each card has a do-by date, and the stock order card is dated first

stages.name: The owners choose together
stages.goal: The owner and co-founder pick card IDs. Ask for the reason when they pass over a top card; record it. The stock card is decided first because the supplier needs 3 weeks.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever a top card was passed over
Both owners' yes is recorded

stages.name: Prepare the stock order
stages.goal: Write the purchase order draft for the chosen quantities and a plan B if it cannot land in time (limit per customer, pre-order wording, hold the promotion back).

outputs.name: Purchase order draft and plan B

checks.name: Delivery date plus the lead time falls before the sale, or plan B is stated
Order value is shown so the owners can check cash before placing it

stages.name: Build the sale pack
stages.goal: Draft the discount setup steps, the email and text schedule staggered so traffic does not arrive in one burst, ad briefs and budgets by day, and the speed and checkout fix steps.

checks.name: No two sends or ad pushes land in the same hour, and the peak hour is below last year's peak traffic or the pages are shown to be lighter
Every discount in the pack keeps margin per order above $18 and is no deeper than 25%
Each discount and speed change says how to undo it
Deadline and stock claims in copy are true and match the stock cover figure

stages.optional_when: No sale pack card was chosen.

stages.name: Prepare support for the surge
stages.goal: Prepare answers and sorting rules for the predictable sale questions (order status, stock, returns, discount codes) and a staffing and escalation note for the weekend.

checks.name: Covers the top 5 ticket topics from last year, or the standard list if no export was given
States who answers within what time, and what gets escalated

stages.name: Place the stock order
stages.goal: The owners place the supplier order after we show quantities, value and delivery date. Record it and track the shipment.

checks.name: Supplier confirmation with quantities and delivery date is on file
Confirmed delivery date is before the sale, or plan B is switched on

stages.name: Apply speed and checkout fixes
stages.goal: The owners apply each approved app cut and theme fix in Shopify admin, then we re-measure and rehearse the sale codes through checkout to the payment step.

outputs.name: Fix receipt with before and after speed

checks.name: Mobile load re-measured after every change, and key pages are at or under the 2.5 s limit or the exception is recorded
Each sale code is applied at checkout on mobile and desktop and the discounted total is correct
A change freeze date is set at least 3 days before the sale

stages.optional_when: No speed or checkout card was chosen.

stages.name: Launch the sale
stages.goal: Registered in advance, the owners switch on each discount, email send and ad change in turn after we show it, and we read back that each is live as designed.

checks.name: Each offer, send and ad change, its time and expected effect are in experiments.jsonl before it goes live
Each live discount, schedule and ad matches the approved pack
Stock levels and limits per customer are set as the stock card says

stages.name: Watch the weekend and read it honestly
stages.goal: Check sales, margin per order, stock cover, speed and tickets every 2 hours through the weekend against the stop rules, then read the weekend against last year's $84,000, the $100,000 target and the market.

checks.name: Each stop rule is read at every check and the result logged
Comparison uses the same weekend span and the same definition of sales as last year's report
Margin per order is computed from order data and cost data, or marked unknown
A change-level claim is made only with at least 100 orders in each compared group; otherwise it is called unproven

stages.name: Keep the playbook
stages.goal: Close each registered change, save rules for the next peak with their scope, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every registered experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each rule says whether it holds for this sale, this store or the playbook

hypotheses.statement: Running out of the top two products by Saturday cost a large part of the gap to $100,000.
hypotheses.test: Hourly units and product-page sessions for the two products before and after sell-out; sales of other products after.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Estimated lost sales are more than $8,400 (10% of last year's weekend), or product-page sessions stayed above 70% of the pre-sell-out level for more than 6 hours.
hypotheses.refute_if: Estimated lost sales are under $1,700 (2%), or shoppers switched to other products at similar value.

hypotheses.test: Conversion rate and orders per 100 sessions during the slow hours compared with the rest of Friday.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Conversion in the slow hours is 20% or more below the rest of Friday on similar traffic.

hypotheses.statement: App scripts and theme weight make the pages too heavy for peak traffic.
hypotheses.test: Mobile largest-content time and script weight on home, collection and top product pages; list of apps.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Any key page loads in more than 2.5 s on mobile, or an app that is not needed for the sale adds script weight.
hypotheses.refute_if: All key pages are at or under 2.5 s with all apps on.

hypotheses.statement: An email send or ad burst arrived all at once and overloaded heavy pages.
hypotheses.test: Sessions per hour against send times and ad spend by hour.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Sessions in the slow hour were at least double the hour before.
hypotheses.refute_if: Sessions rose gradually, under 50% per hour.

hypotheses.statement: The deepest allowed discount (25%) drops margin per order below $18 on some products.
hypotheses.test: Margin per order at 10, 15, 20 and 25% off for the top products, from unit and shipping costs.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Margin per order is below $18 at 25% off for any of the top products.
hypotheses.refute_if: Margin per order stays above $18 at 25% off for all of them.

hypotheses.statement: Stock for the top two products cannot be reordered in time unless the order is placed within about a week.
hypotheses.test: Sale date minus 21 days minus today, against stock cover and forecast demand.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Forecast demand in the expected case exceeds on-hand plus incoming stock.
hypotheses.refute_if: On-hand plus incoming covers the high case.

hypotheses.statement: Support was overwhelmed during the sale, hurting repeat buyers.
hypotheses.test: Tickets per hour and first reply time from the Gorgias export.
hypotheses.confirm_if: First reply time exceeded 24 hours for more than a quarter of sale-weekend tickets.
hypotheses.refute_if: Most tickets were answered within 12 hours.

hypotheses.statement: $100,000 needs more than recovery of last year's losses: demand has to grow faster than the market.
hypotheses.test: Compare required growth (about 19%) with the market's reported growth (about 9%) and the diagnosis's recovered-sales estimate.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Recovered sales explain less than $8,000 of the $16,000 gap.
hypotheses.refute_if: Recovered sales explain at least $12,000 of the gap.

measurement.window: The full Black Friday weekend, checked every 2 hours, then the 7 days after; compare with last year's same-length weekend and the 4 weeks before as the normal-week baseline.
measurement.min_volume: At least 100 orders in each compared group before any single change is credited; otherwise the verdict is unproven.
measurement.stop_rule: Pull back a discount at once if margin per order for that product falls below $18; limit or pause promotion of a product when stock cover is under 24 hours of expected sales; pause ad pushes if mobile load goes over 4 s; otherwise run the full weekend.
